plate_solver.title: Plate Solver

help.ExposureTime: Exposure time, in seconds, used for the images taken by the plate solver. Longer exposures pick up more stars, which helps with solving faint or sparse fields, but slow down each solve attempt.
help.Gain: Camera gain used for plate-solving exposures. Leave empty to use the camera's default gain.
help.ASTAPLocation: Path to the ASTAP executable (astap.exe) on the system running NINA. Required for local plate solving with ASTAP.
help.SearchRadius: Radius in degrees around the target coordinates that the solver searches when attempting a blind solve. A larger radius increases solve time but helps when the mount's initial position is less accurate.
help.Threshold: Maximum allowed deviation, in arcminutes, between the solved position and the target during Slew & Center. If the solve is farther off than this, another slew-and-solve cycle is triggered.
help.RotationTolerance: Maximum allowed rotation deviation, in degrees, between the solved image orientation and the target orientation during Center & Rotate. If exceeded, the rotator is adjusted and the frame is re-solved.
help.MaxObjects: Maximum number of stars the plate solver uses for matching. Lower values solve faster but may reduce accuracy on sparse fields; higher values improve reliability at the cost of speed.
help.NumberOfAttempts: Maximum number of times the plate solver retries a failed solve before giving up.
help.ReattemptDelay: Delay, in minutes, before the plate solver starts a new attempt after a failed solve.
help.BlindFailoverEnabled: If a regular plate solve fails, automatically fall back to a blind solve (no initial coordinates needed) instead of aborting.

phd2.fastRecenter: Fast recenter after calibration or dither

help.fastRecenter: During calibration or dithering the mount can move far from the lock position. If on, PHD2 moves back as fast as possible to save time — completely optional. If calibration often fails because the star snaps back too quickly, turn it off (often a sign of large polar-alignment or periodic error).
help.mountGuideOutput: Lets PHD2 actually send guide commands to the mount. Normally on; turn it off only if you want to observe the mount's uncorrected behaviour.
help.searchRegion: Size of the tracking rectangle in pixels (a radius — 15 means a 30×30 box). Increase it if the mount tracks poorly or isn't well polar-aligned; too large a region can catch multiple stars and hurt guiding.
help.minStarHFD: Smallest half-flux-diameter (the 'size') a star must have to be used as guide star — the best way to stop PHD2 locking onto clumps of hot pixels. Default ~1.5 suits most setups; raise it only if real faint stars get rejected.
help.maxStarHFD: Largest half-flux-diameter a guide star may have; bloated or out-of-focus blobs above this are ignored during selection.
help.massChangeEnabled: Monitors the guide star's brightness and size versus the background. Deprecated — usually best left off; enable only to be sure PHD2 doesn't switch to a nearby star.
help.massChangeThreshold: With Star Mass Detection on, PHD2 reports a lost star if the star's brightness or size changes more than this percent. Increase it (or disable detection) if you get frequent 'star lost – mass change' errors while the star is clearly visible.
help.minStarSNR: Minimum SNR a star needs to be auto-selected (non-saturated stars). Change only if experienced — too high a value means no star gets picked; refreshing the dark library or using longer exposures is usually better.
help.useMultipleStars: Guides on several stars at once instead of just one, which improves stability. Not available when sub-frames are used.
help.autoSelectDownsample: For rare cases where auto-selection fails because the stars look misshapen. Leave on 'Auto'; values above 1 can improve recognition.
help.saturationByADU: How PHD2 detects saturated stars so it can avoid them. 'By ADU value' uses the brightness reported by the sensor (recommended); the alternative judges saturation from the star-profile shape and is less accurate.
help.saturationADUValue: Pixel value at which a star counts as saturated (8-bit cameras ≈ 255, 16-bit ≈ 65535). If unsure, set it to your camera's maximum pixel value.
help.cameraGain: Guide-camera gain as a percentage of the camera's range (e.g. 50% maps to gain 60 on a 40–80 camera). Lower gain reduces noise; it usually doesn't need changing once your setup is stable.
help.cameraBinning: Hardware binning for guide exposures — raises sensitivity and speeds downloads at the cost of resolution. Use a separate PHD2 profile for each binning value.
help.focalLength: Focal length of the guide scope in millimetres. With the pixel size it sets the image scale and lets PHD2 report guiding in arc-seconds, so set it correctly.
help.calibrationStep: Length of each guide pulse during calibration. Aim for a value giving 8–14 steps in each direction, and calibrate near the celestial equator (declination ≈ 0).
help.restoreCalibration: Automatically reloads the latest calibration when equipment connects (good for ASCOM/INDI or aux-mount setups). If you use it, the guide camera must not be rotated relative to the scope or sky.
help.assumeDecOrthogonal: PHD2 normally measures the camera angle for RA and Dec independently. Force the Dec angle perpendicular to RA to help with very high periodic error, large Dec backlash or poor seeing.
help.useDecCompensation: Automatically adjusts the RA guide rate for the current declination (needs an ASCOM/INDI mount connection). Leave on except in unusual cases. Not the same as declination backlash compensation.
help.reverseDecAfterFlip: Tells PHD2 how to adjust calibration after a meridian flip. Leave off if guiding is normal after a flip; turn it on and recalibrate only if you see run-away guiding in declination afterwards.
help.guideAlgorithm: Selects the guiding algorithm for this axis. Hysteresis weighs recent corrections against the latest deflection; ResistSwitch resists direction changes (good for Dec backlash); LowPass/LowPass2 are conservative choices for good mounts; Predictive PEC (PPEC) models and pre-corrects periodic error (RA); ZFilter works in the frequency domain. Defaults suit most users.

algo.minMove: Smallest star deflection (in pixels) that triggers a guide correction; smaller moves are ignored to avoid chasing seeing. This is the parameter most worth tuning per night for the conditions.
algo.maxMove: Largest single guide correction allowed, in pixels; caps over-reaction to a spurious large jump.
algo.aggression: How strongly each measured error is corrected, in percent. 100% applies the full correction; lower values (e.g. 60%) correct less to avoid over-shoot. Lower is safer.
algo.hysteresis: Weight given to the history of recent corrections versus the latest frame, in percent. Higher values smooth the corrections but react more slowly to a genuine change of direction.
algo.predictiveWeight: Predictive PEC: weight of the predicted (modelled) part of the correction. Defaults suit most mounts; large changes can worsen guiding.
algo.reactiveWeight: Predictive PEC: weight of the reactive part, based on the star's displacement in the latest frame. Defaults suit most mounts.
algo.periodLength: Predictive PEC: length of the mount's worm period in seconds. PHD2 uses it to model and pre-correct the recurring RA error. Take it from the mount's specification (about 479 s for an EQ6) or read it off the PEC peak in the guiding FFT.
algo.slopeWeight: LowPass: how much the recent trend (slope) of star movement influences the correction, in percent. Keeps the algorithm from being too sluggish; 0 uses only the median of recent history.
algo.expFactor: ZFilter: the virtual exposure time equals the real exposure × this factor. Higher values filter more seeing (smoother but slower); a virtual exposure of ~2–4 s is a good starting point for RA.

help.ditherMode: How PHD2 computes each dither. Random picks a random size and direction; Spiral uses fixed-size steps in a clockwise spiral — useful when the imaging camera has fixed-pattern noise or the mount has troublesome Dec backlash.
help.ditherRaOnly: Dither only along the RA axis. Useful when Dec guiding is off or the mount has significant Dec backlash.
help.ditherScale: Multiplier applied to the dither amount requested by the imaging application — increase it for larger dithers, decrease for smaller.
help.backlashAmount: Length of the extra correction pulse (in ms) PHD2 adds on a DEC direction reversal. PHD2 auto-tunes this between Min and Max.
help.backlashEnabled: Compensates for DEC backlash by adding an extra pulse when the mount reverses direction. Helpful for mounts with noticeable gear backlash; leave off if your mount guides cleanly in DEC.
help.backlashMax: Upper limit (ms) for the auto-adjusted backlash pulse amount.
help.backlashMin: Lower limit (ms) for the auto-adjusted backlash pulse amount.

darkLibrary.title: Dark Library
darkLibrary.info: Build a dark library by capturing dark frames at different exposure times. PHD2 uses these to subtract sensor noise from guide frames.
darkLibrary.warning: Building blocks PHD2 — all other PHD2 actions are disabled while a build is running.
darkLibrary.invalidRange: Min exposure must be less than or equal to max exposure
darkLibrary.buildActiveMessage: PHD2 actions are blocked until the build completes.

help.focusStdError: σ(focus): the standard error of the best-focus position, in focuser steps, propagated from the hyperbolic fit. It is the parametric uncertainty estimate (it assumes the model is correct and the measurement errors are Gaussian) and the quantity that most directly shows how well the run pinned down focus. Smaller is better. Shown as -- only when the fit is too degenerate to localize focus, for example a near-monotonic curve. The error bar on the final focus point in the chart shows this value, or the leave-one-out stability when it is unavailable.
help.hyperbolicModel: The hyperbolic model used to fit this run. For a fixed model it is that model; for the Hybrid (Best Fit) option it is the concrete model selected for this run, the one with the least expected error for the best-focus position.
help.starsDetected: The fewest and the most stars detected at any single focuser position the focus curve was actually fitted on. Points the fit discarded (outliers rejected by the curve fit, and points outside the symmetric focus window) are left out, so this describes the data the result rests on. A low range means the curve was built from thin measurements and its best-focus position will move more from run to run; a high one means the run had plenty of signal. Star counts naturally fall away from focus, so the minimum is normally one of the outermost points of the sweep.

pins_settings.title: PINS TPPA Settings
pins_settings.help_default_move_rate: The maximum slew speed of the mount in degrees per second. TPPA uses this value to calculate how fast to move between measurement points. It is important that this matches your mount's actual maximum speed. Some mount vendors implement the move rate differently - if your mount doesn't move the expected distance, adjust the Move Timeout Factor.
pins_settings.help_default_east_direction: Defines if the direction for the second and third measurement points should be done by moving in east or west direction along the RA axis. Some mount drivers may need this reversed in the telescope tab settings.
pins_settings.help_move_timeout_factor: After (Target Distance / Move Rate × Timeout Factor) seconds, the mount will stop moving as a failsafe. Only increase this if you get warnings that the target distance was not reached.
pins_settings.help_default_target_distance: The distance in degrees between measurement points during the polar alignment procedure.
pins_settings.help_default_search_radius: The search radius in degrees for your plate solver during TPPA. Should be larger than your initial polar alignment error, but not too large to ensure quick solves.
pins_settings.help_default_azimuth_offset: The azimuth offset in degrees from the pole position to start from for the first measurement point.
pins_settings.help_default_altitude_offset: The altitude offset in degrees from the pole position to start from for the first measurement point.
pins_settings.help_alignment_tolerance: When set to a non-zero value, the polar alignment routine automatically completes when the error is below this tolerance (in arcminutes).
pins_settings.help_refraction_adjustment: When enabled, the application will factor in atmospheric refraction based on your location, elevation and current weather conditions. Uses standard atmospheric parameters if no weather source is connected.
pins_settings.help_stop_tracking_when_done: When enabled, the mount will stop tracking after polar alignment is finished. Disable if you want your mount to continue tracking.
pins_settings.help_settle_time: When using automated adjustments, specifies the amount of time in seconds to wait after each movement.
pins_settings.help_auto_pause: Automatic pause setting for the polar alignment procedure.
pins_settings.help_log_error: When enabled, a log file will be created with the polar alignment error adjustments and continuous errors after each adjustment.

help.starsInModel: The number of stars used in the sensor model. Each star needs to be matched across at least 5 of the frames, and some star fits are rejected as outliers during modeling.
help.tilt: The angle the sensor is tilted. 0 indicates no tilt, and values here are typically very small
help.curvatureRadius: Near focus, the base of the sensor parabola is close to a sphere. This value represents the radius of that sphere. Larger values indicate flatter curves, which are better.
help.curvatureEffect: The nominal distance from the corner of the sensor to the center, due purely to the modeled curvature. Curvature effect is more exaggerated on larger sensors.
help.tiltEffect: The maximum nominal distance from the corners of the sensor to the center, due purely to the modeled tilt.
help.meanFocuserPosition: The weighted mean focuser position under the sensor curve, which serves as a focus point where pixels throughout the sensor have minimum absolute distance from optimal focus
help.autoFocusOffset: The number of focuser steps between the AutoFocus position and the Sensor Mean Focuser Position. You can set this value in the AF Offset setting in Auto Focus Options.
help.criticalFocus: The focuser distance a pixel can be from optimal focus before the effects can be noticed. This value increases with larger (slower) F/ratios, which can tolerate more curvature before affecting image quality
help.reducedChiSquared: Reduced χ² measures how well the model fits the per-star best-focus positions relative to their estimated uncertainties (≈1 means it fits within measurement error). The per-star σ is approximate and does not capture model error, so reduced χ² routinely runs far above 1 even for good fits and its absolute scale is rig-dependent. It is shown for information and is only used as a rejection criterion when the R² is also very low.

optimizer.title: Optimize Star Detection
optimizer.timedOutNotice: The previous optimization was closed after 30 minutes without activity, to free its frames. Starting a new one.
optimizer.replayIntro: Choose a saved auto-focus run to tune star detection against. The optimizer re-runs detection on its frames with many parameter combinations and keeps the settings that best pin down focus.
optimizer.liveIntro: This moves the focuser across a fixed sweep centered on the current position and saves an image at each step, then finds the star-detection settings that build the best focus curve from them. It does not try to reach focus itself, so it works even when your current settings cannot. Make sure your camera is already approximately in focus.
optimizer.startFromCurrent: Start from my current settings (refine them further)
optimizer.forInspection: Optimize for aberration inspection (favor more stars)
optimizer.noSavedRuns: No saved auto-focus runs found. Turn on saving in the AutoFocus options and run an auto-focus first, or use a live sweep.
optimizer.sequenceRunningLive: A sequence is running, so a live sweep is disabled: it would move the focuser and take exposures in the middle of it. A saved auto-focus run works meanwhile.
optimizer.runsInBackground: You can close this window: the optimization keeps running in NINA, and you can reopen it from the Star Detection tab.
optimizer.captureNewSweep: Capture a new sweep and optimize
optimizer.acceptHint: Accept applies the selected settings as your active star-detection settings. Close discards them.
optimizer.reviewDesktopOnly: Reviewing and labelling frames is only available in the desktop wizard.

help.sourceMode: Live (the default) triggers a fresh auto-focus that saves its frames, then optimizes against those. Replay optimizes against an auto-focus run you have already saved.
help.targetFilter: Per-filter star detection is enabled, so this run tunes ONE filter's settings set. The baseline and 'current settings' come from this filter's set; a live sweep moves the wheel to this filter and exposes through it; and Accept writes the optimized result into this filter's set.
help.optimizeMode: Optimize runs the parameter search and recommends improved settings. Use current settings skips the search entirely and jumps straight to a summary built from your current settings, so you can review (and label) today's detection without an optimization pass. Either way, after reviewing you can still run Optimize with feedback to recover the stars you labeled.
help.startFromCurrent: When checked, the optimizer SEEDS from your current settings instead of the fully-default settings, so it refines your existing setup rather than re-deriving from scratch. Useful when you've already hand-tuned detection and want incremental improvement. The search still only accepts changes that improve on your current settings, and improvement is reported against them. Leave unchecked to explore from the defaults (recommended for a first run). Only applies in Optimize mode.
help.donutDetection: When checked, the optimizer is allowed to recover out-of-focus DONUT stars — heavily defocused stars that appear as hollow rings — which the detector otherwise drops (they fragment or fail the fill-ratio test). It also unlocks diffraction-spike and saturated-bloom suppression so a bright star's rays aren't mistaken for stars. Recommended for telescopes with a central obstruction (Newtonians/SCTs) whose defocused stars become donuts; leave OFF for refractors (defocused stars are filled disks, not rings). Saved to your profile and default OFF. When OFF, star detection is exactly as before.
help.forInspection: When checked, the optimizer favors detecting MANY MORE stars spread across the frame, which the aberration inspector needs to measure sensor tilt and field curvature. It does this by trading away a little auto-focus-curve sharpness for star count — but the fit is bounded: settings that make the focus curve noticeably worse than your current settings are penalized, so focus stays usable. Leave OFF to optimize purely for the tightest auto-focus curve (the default). Only applies in Optimize mode; nothing is saved until you Accept.
help.gpuAcceleration: Run this wizard's star detection pipeline on a CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU when one is present, typically speeding optimization up 2-3x. Only this wizard uses the GPU: auto focus, sensor modeling, and regular star detection always run on the CPU. This is a per-computer setting (it is not exported or shared per-filter), it persists immediately, and it is skipped automatically when no suitable GPU is found or frames are too small to benefit. Applies the next time a run is loaded.
help.detectionBinningRec: Recommended from this run's fitted in-focus HFR, using the detector's 2 to 4 pixel calibration target. Optimize again re-runs the search on the same frames at the recommended factor; nothing is saved until you Accept, which applies the factor and the re-tuned settings together.
help.focusRecovery: Widens the live sweep by this many extra steps on EACH side, so the auto-focus curve can still bracket focus when you start well off focus. The extra far-from-focus frames are down-weighted in the fit and exempt from the star-count requirements, so they help find focus without skewing it. Set 0 to disable recovery.
help.liveExposure: The exposure for every frame of the sweep, starting from your profile's auto-focus exposure. Make it long enough that stars stay visible out at the defocused ends of the sweep. Narrowband filters usually need a longer exposure to start. After a good result you can adopt this exposure into your profile from the summary.
help.variant: Switch the chart and the summary below between your current settings, the optimized settings, and (after Optimize with feedback) the feedback-optimized settings. Accept applies whichever variant is shown (Current can't be accepted — it's your baseline).
help.starSignal: Brightness Sensitivity is the acceptance gate a candidate must clear to count as a star: its brightness above the local background, divided by the local noise. It ranges from 0 to 50 and the shipped default is 10, so a value near the bottom means almost anything above the noise was admitted — whether the optimizer landed there or you set it by hand. The recommended exposure is what would put this run's stars back at the default gate, assuming sky noise dominates, so quadrupling the exposure doubles S/N. It scales from the exposure the run's own frames were captured with, or from your profile's auto-focus exposure when the frames record none. One run never recommends more than 30 s per frame, and derives at most 4x the current exposure before that number is rounded up to a practical exposure-time step — which can land the shown value a little past 4x, but never past 30 s.
help.applyStepSize: When checked, clicking Accept also writes the recommended auto-focus step size and offset steps to the active profile, and for a live sweep the exposure it captured with. The step size is sized so a sweep lands several measurement points across the focus-sensitive region of the curve. When per-filter star detection is enabled, the step size, offset steps and live sweep exposure all go to the TARGET FILTER instead of the profile, so optimizing one filter no longer overwrites the settings every other filter uses. Disabled when these already match your current settings (nothing to apply).
help.continue: Run another optimization pass starting from the settings just found, giving the search a fresh chance to refine further (it resets its step sizes, so it can make larger moves again). Useful when the last pass looks like it stopped just short. Limited to 3 total passes; the Changed parameters table shows the value of each setting after every pass.

aberrationInspectorOptions.resetPrompt: Reset all Aberration Inspector options to their defaults? This cannot be undone.
aberrationInspectorOptions.autoFromDriver: Automatic: {value} µm/step from the focuser driver
aberrationInspectorOptions.noDriverStepSize: The focuser driver does not report a step size, so micron readouts are hidden. Enter your focuser's step size to enable them.

help.stepCount: The minimum number of data points needed on each side of the AutoFocus curve minimum. Uses the value set for AutoFocus if blank
help.stepSize: How many focuser steps in between each data point when doing an AutoFocus. Uses the value set for AutoFocus if blank — the current filter's per-filter sweep override when per-filter star detection defines one, otherwise the profile's Auto Focus Step Size.
help.framesPerPoint: How many exposures to average together for each focuser point. Uses the value set for AutoFocus if blank
help.detailedAnalysisExposureSeconds: How long of an exposure to take for detailed analysis. Defaults to the Auto Focus exposure duration if not set
help.simpleExposureSeconds: Take a single exposure to produce a FWHM contour map and Eccentricity vector field
help.timeoutSeconds: How long, in seconds, after which AutoFocus should time out and fail. Uses the value set for AutoFocus if blank
help.signalAmplification: Increases the resolution and signal of sensor-model / tilt calibration runs by capturing more, finer-spaced focuser points. The focuser step size is divided by this factor and the number of steps multiplied by it, so the sweep covers the same range with more points (and smaller defocus jumps between adjacent frames, which makes star alignment more reliable). Default 1 (off). Raise it for faint fields or poor seeing; each step multiplies the exposures per sweep. Applies to live captures only, not when replaying saved frames.
help.centerFocuserBeforeRun: When on, a quick standard AutoFocus is run before each live sensor-model / tilt calibration sweep to center the focuser at best focus. The detailed sweep then brackets focus symmetrically, which reduces extreme one-sided defocus frames that fail to align. Off by default; it adds an extra AutoFocus run to every sweep. Has no effect when replaying saved frames.
help.numRegionsWide: How many cells wide to divide the sensor pixels when generating a grid of eccentricity vectors. This value must be an odd, positive integer, and the height will be calculated proportionally from it based on the sensor resolution
help.eccentricityColorMapEnabled: Enable color on the eccentricity map
help.interpolationEnabled: Use interpolated points evenly spaced along a grid instead of the individual stars themselves. This should improve consistency of results and prevent overfitting where there are more stars.
help.sensorCurveModelEnabled: In addition to analyzing AutoFocus curves for the corners and center, create a paraboloid model of the sensor by creating focus curves for every star. This enables calculation of centering error and curvature, and is similar to the type of analysis done by CCD Inspector
help.micronsPerFocuserStep: How much the focuser moves per step, in microns — the scale that turns every focuser measurement into microns. Leave this blank to use the value your focuser driver reports (shown greyed out in the box); type a value to override it. If neither is available, micron readouts are hidden rather than guessed.
help.sensorROI: Uses only a centered portion of the full sensor when evaluating aberration. This is useful if you have a flattener that cannot produce a flat field for your sensor.
help.cornersROI: Reduces the size of the corner regions when performing corners analysis. This can be useful if you want to evaluate only stars closer to the corners than the full 1/9th region. This can be combined with Sensor ROI.
help.fixedSensorCenter: Assume the sensor is perfectly centered in the optical train. If this option is off, the sensor location will be modeled along with the other model parameters.
help.stepSizeMismatch: Your focuser step size differs from what the driver reports by more than 1%. This is informational — your value is the one being used, and if you measured it yourself it is probably the better one. It is worth a look because some drivers report this field wrongly (a common case reports 1, meaning one step per step rather than one micron per step). Clear the box to use the driver's value instead.
help.frameReviewEnabled: When on, the per-frame images from a Sensor Curve Model run are retained in memory so the "Review Frames" button can show each frame with its detected stars, HFRs, and cross-frame registration. Requires the Sensor Curve Model to be enabled. Increases memory use while the run's results are kept (the frames are released when you clear the analysis, start a new run, or close the review window). Off by default.
help.useRANSAC: When on, each frame's stars are aligned to the reference frame (using a RANSAC similarity transform) before they are matched, correcting for small drift, rotation, or flexure between exposures in the autofocus run. Enable this when there is movement between frames; it allows stars to be matched with a tighter search radius and generally produces a more reliable model.
help.useAffineAlignment: When off (default), images are aligned with a 4-DOF similarity transform (translation, rotation, uniform scale), which is the physically correct model for a single autofocus run and gives more robust, repeatable results. Enable only to diagnose alignment by allowing the less-constrained 6-DOF affine transform (adds shear and anisotropic scale).
help.rejectBadlyFittingMatches: When on, measurement points that fit poorly to a star's hyperbolic focus curve are iteratively rejected before that star's best-focus position is used, so a few bad measurements do not bias the result. Slightly increases per-star fitting time.
help.astigmaticCurvatureEnabled: When off (default), field curvature is modeled as rotationally symmetric (a single curvature coefficient), which fits a typical refractor or reflector. Enable to fit independent X and Y curvature, representing the saddle-shaped field of an astigmatic optical train. Adds one free parameter to the surface fit.
help.rejectBadBrightnessMatches: When on, candidate star matches whose relative brightness differs by more than the brightness tolerance are rejected, reducing mismatches in crowded fields. The tolerance is searched automatically, starting from the 'Starting Brightness Tolerance' value.
help.acceptableRSquaredMin: The smallest R² (fraction of best-focus variance explained) the model may have before its low R² is allowed to contribute to rejection. On its own a low R² never rejects the model — a near-flat sensor legitimately scores a low R². The model is rejected only when R² falls below this value AND the reduced χ² is also high (above a fixed sanity cap of 5).
help.startingBrightnessDiff: If set, this value is used as the starting point for the automatic search that finds a brightness tolerance giving a good set of matched stars across all regions of all images. Leave this blank to start from a fixed default.
help.showSensorModel: Shows the fitted sensor model (tilt and curvature) alongside the analysis results. Only available while the Sensor Curve Model is enabled.
help.interpolationAlgo: The radial basis function used to interpolate the eccentricity/FWHM contour maps between measured grid cells.
help.interpolationAmount: How much smoothing the contour interpolation applies.

autoFocusOptions.resetPrompt: Reset all AutoFocus options to their defaults? This cannot be undone.

help.maxConcurrent: The maximum number of auto focus images that can be processed at the same time. This is useful if processing time is much longer than exposure time and your system has limited memory or cores. 0 represents no limit.
help.autoFocusTimeoutSeconds: How long an Auto Focus operation can take before we cancel it and move on.
help.focuserOffset: Advanced Only! Moves the focuser this fixed amount at the end of an AutoFocus
help.maxBlindStepsPerDirection: Maximum number of blind AutoFocus steps attempted in each direction before reversing to try the other side. Set to 0 to disable the cap.
help.focuserIncreasesTowardObjective: Which way your focuser travels: does a HIGHER focuser position move the camera away from the objective (standard), or toward it (reversed)? This affects direction LABELS AND DIAGRAMS ONLY — the "move toward/away from the objective" captions, the Telescope/Sensor labels on the sensor model, the spacer advice, and the up/down motion arrows in the tilt guidance. It can never change a measurement, a screw angle, or a correction: the tilt adapter's direction is measured in focuser units, and the focuser convention cancels out of that measurement entirely. So if these labels read backwards on your rig, flip this — nothing you have already calibrated is affected, and nothing will start turning the other way.
help.validateHfrImprovement: If enabled, takes an extra exposure before and after to ensure HFR improved. This check may be done in addition to the R² validation configured in NINA's Auto Focus options.
help.hfrImprovementThreshold: How much wiggle room when validating HFR improvements. The default value of 15% means that the Auto Focus fails if the initial HFR is 15% or more better than the final HFR
help.hyperbolicFitModel: Which hyperbolic model is fit to the focus curve. Hybrid (Best Fit) is the recommended default: the curve is rendered live with the Tilted Hyperbola, then at run completion every model is refit and the one with the least expected error for the best-focus position is kept — so each run self-selects its most trustworthy fit. The fixed choices: Symmetric is the classic 4-parameter hyperbola; the others are asymmetric (different slope on either side of focus, common because out-of-focus HFR behaves differently than in-focus): Tilted Hyperbola is a single smooth curve with a linear skew, Smooth Blend smoothly blends two hyperbolas, and Uneven Blend is the original blended fit.
help.weightedHyperbolicFitEnabled: Weights each point in the hyperbolic fit based on measurement error. σ values are regularized before fitting: a degenerate near-zero σ (e.g. from a frame with very few detected stars) is floored at 20% of the sweep's median σ, and an unknown σ gets the median, so no single point can dominate the fit through a degenerate error estimate.
help.fitRejectionCriterion: Which goodness-of-fit metric decides whether an auto-focus run is rejected. R² (default) keeps the existing behavior, rejecting when the fit's R² falls below NINA's R² threshold (Focuser settings). Reduced χ² instead rejects when the hyperbolic fit's reduced χ² exceeds the threshold below — a scatter-units goodness-of-fit bound for a focus curve, but it is only valid when 'Weighted Hyperbolic Fit' is enabled (it relies on per-point measurement σ). Quadratic and trendline fits always use R² regardless of this setting.
help.rSquaredRejectionThreshold: The minimum R² (coefficient of determination) below which an auto-focus run is rejected, when the rejection criterion is set to R². This is NINA's own R² threshold from the Focuser settings; editing it here changes that same profile setting. R² closer to 1 indicates a better fit to the measured focus curve.
help.reducedChiSquaredRejectionThreshold: Upper bound on the hyperbolic fit's reduced χ² (χ² per degree of freedom) above which the run is rejected, when the rejection criterion is set to Reduced χ². The per-point σ behind the weights is the star-ensemble scatter, which overstates the uncertainty of the per-point median HFR — so reduced χ² typically runs well below 1, shrinks as more stars are detected, and grows as Frames Per Point increases. Treat this threshold as a coarse sanity bound rather than a calibrated statistical test. Set to 0 to disable. Meaningful only with weighted fits.
help.maxOutlierRejections: Controls the maximum number of points that can be rejected as outliers during Auto Focus curve fitting.
help.outlierRejectionConfidence: Confidence level for a two-tailed Grubbs statistical test of outliers to use during Auto Focus curve fitting. 95% is a reasonable default. Must be above 50% and below 100%.
help.save: Saves details about every Auto Focus run, including a copy of the image, the star detection results, and the stretched annotated image
help.keepFramesForReview: When on, the per-frame images from an auto-focus run started here in the AutoFocus pane — a live run or a Replay Saved AF — are kept in memory so the "Review Frames" button can show each frame with its detected stars and HFRs. Only applies to runs from this pane — auto-focus during an imaging sequence never keeps frames (it would use too much memory). The frames are released when you start a new run or close the review window. Off by default; saved in your profile.

starDetection.perFilterActive: Per-filter star detection is enabled in HocusFocus. These settings belong to the filter currently selected for editing there, not to the global profile settings.
starDetection.resetPrompt: Reset all Star Detection options to their defaults? This cannot be undone.
starDetection.optimizerDescription: Tune star detection against a saved or live auto-focus run, and optionally apply the result as your Simple-Mode settings.

help.advancedMode: Enables advanced mode with fine-grained control over star detection parameters. Not recommended unless you're an expert
help.useHotpixelThresholding: A more sophisticated version of hotpixel filtering that limits pixel replacement to those where the median is far off of the pixel value. This prevents the whole image from being blurred, which can have a negative effect on HFR and PSF measurement accuracy
help.useAutoFocusCrop: Uses the inner and outer crop from the Auto Focus options for regular exposures (ie, those that aren't done during focusing)
help.fitPSF: Whether to fit PSF models to detected stars. This is required for FWHM and Eccentricity
help.debugMode: Enables debug mode, which saves additional data useful for debugging. Keep this off unless you're tuning star detection and want to view structure maps.
help.detectionBinning: Software binning applied to the frame for star detection only. Star detection is calibrated for in-focus stars of roughly 2 to 4 pixels; at long focal lengths stars are much larger than that, which puts the pixel-based settings out of range. Binning the frame for detection brings star size back into range and improves signal to noise per pixel. The image you see and the HFR values reported stay at the resolution the camera captured. This is not NINA's Auto Focus Binning, which changes how the camera captures the auto-focus frames and should match the binning you image at; the two multiply
help.measurementAverage: Controls how the average star measurement across the frame is calculated. Median is robust to outliers, and is the default.
help.useOptimizedSettings: When enabled, the optimized star-detection settings produced by the optimization wizard drive detection instead of the Noise Level / Pixel Scale / Focus Range presets. Only available in Simple Mode after the wizard has produced and applied a result
help.noiseLevel: Controls the amount of blurring done on the source image before beginning the star detection process. Increase this if you have a particularly noisy sensor or shoot at a very high focal ratio
help.pixelScale: At high focal lengths, pixel scale decreases and apparent star size (in pixels) increases. Setting this to a higher focal length increases the number of layers considered for star detection, which could increase false positives due from nebulosity
help.focusRange: As you get further from critical focus, stars become large donuts. Star detection will typically consider them too large to be stars when you're far enough from focus. Enabling a wide range increases the number of layers considered for star detection
help.hotpixelFiltering: Uses a 3x3 box median convolution to filter out hotpixels. This should be on, unless you're working with a calibrated image with hotpixels removed
help.noiseReducedStarMeasurement: Apply noise detection settings to the pixels used during star measurement. By default, it is applied only to the structure detection image.
help.noiseReductionRadius: Blurs the image with a NxN gaussian convolution and a sigma automatically chosen to match this radius. Larger values blur the image further. If this is enabled, hotpixel filtering is automatically performed before to prevent the hotpixels from bleeding into the surrounding pixels
help.noiseClippingMultiplier: Structure map generation binarizes pixels above the noise floor after noise detection and before star detection. This floor is calculated based on the background (median of the whole image) + this multiplier times the noise standard deviation, as calculated using the Kappa-Sigma algorithm. When Locally Adaptive Binarization is enabled (the default), the background median and noise are measured locally per region rather than across the whole image. Increasing this value more aggressively clips the background, which can be useful if star bounding boxes include too much background data.
help.starClippingMultiplier: Number of noise standard deviations above the local background median to filter star candidate pixels out from star consideration and HFR analysis. The noise level is measured on the image actually used for star measurement, so this value means the same thing regardless of noise-reduction settings. Decrease this if there are a large number of stars excluded for being degenerate and you can see many clear dim stars that are not detected.
help.structureLayers: The number of dyadic (power of 2) layers to include in structure detection. At the default of 4 (2⁴=16), structures larger than 16 pixels in size are excluded from structure detection
help.brightnessSensitivity: Given a star with a normalized brightness measure of s, a local background of b, and a background noise level of n, star sensitivity is measured as the ratio of the star brightness above the background relative to the background noise, (s-b)/n. The noise level n is measured on the image actually used for star measurement, so this value is an honest multiple of the real noise and means the same thing regardless of noise-reduction settings. If you find a large number of rejections due to low sensitivity, smaller values increase sensitivity.
help.locallyAdaptiveBinarization: Makes the structure-map binarization threshold spatially adaptive. Normally a single global threshold (background median + Noise Clipping Multiplier × global noise σ) is applied across the whole frame, which is too high in clean regions (losing faint stars) and too low in noisy corners (admitting noise). When enabled, the threshold becomes a smooth surface computed from robust local statistics on a coarse block grid — local background median + Noise Clipping Multiplier × local noise σ — so the same Noise Clipping Multiplier is locally fair everywhere. Recovers faint real stars in clean regions while rejecting noise in vignetted/gradient-heavy corners. On by default; turn it off to revert to the single global threshold, which makes detection bit-for-bit identical to the legacy behavior. EARLY-stage setting.
help.adaptiveNoiseBlockSize: Only used while Locally Adaptive Binarization is on. The side length (in pixels) of the square blocks the local median/noise surface is estimated on. Larger values give a smoother, cheaper surface with less local adaptivity; smaller values adapt more finely but produce a noisier surface and risk absorbing real extended structure (large defocused donuts) into the background. The sane range is 64–256. Default 128.
help.starPeakResponse: The ratio of the star median relative to the star peak. It provides a measure of flatness, since median values close to the peak indicate low dispersion. Consider increasing if too many stars are rejected with "Too Flat"
help.maxDistortion: A MINIMUM fill ratio, despite the name: the ratio of star pixels to the area of the bounding box, where a candidate is rejected as Too Distorted when its fill ratio falls BELOW this value. Raising it makes the gate stricter, not looser. A perfectly round star fills PI/4, approximately 0.785, so values above that reject every round star. The default of 0.5 allows for some distortion and measurement error and should work for most cases.
help.starCenterTolerance: Size (as a percentage) of a centered rectangle within the star bounding box that the star center must be in. 1.0 covers the whole region, and 0.0 will fail every star
help.starBackgroundBoxExpansion: The background is estimated by looking in an area around the star bounding box, increased on each side by this number of pixels. The default value of 3 should work for most cases, but you can consider increasing it if stars are very spare, or even decreasing it if the star field is very crowded with stars less than 3 pixels from one another.
help.minStarBoundingBoxSize: The minimum allowed size (length of either side) of a star candidate's bounding box. Increasing this can be helpful at very high focal lengths if too many small structures are detected
help.minHFR: Minimum HFR for a star to be considered viable
help.structureDilationSize: During star detection a structure map is generated containing potential star pixels that are above the background noise threshold. This parameter defines the size of gaussian morphology filter used to dilate the structure map. Consider increasing this value if bounding boxes are not large enough around stars, which may be more likely at very high focal lengths.
help.structureDilationCount: This parameter is related to Structure Dilation Size. It specifies the number of times the morphological dilation is performed. Consider increasing this value if bounding boxes are not large enough around stars, which may be more likely at very high focal lengths.
help.pixelSampleSize: When calculating star centers and HFR, we sample values between pixels using bilinear interpolation to improve accuracy. The optimal sample size depends on whether and how much your optical system is undersampling. Increase to 1 if you are perfectly- or over-sampled, and consider lowering it below 0.5 if you are more than 2x undersampled. This value must be between 25 and 100, inclusive
help.defocusAwareGates: When enabled, both the Max Distortion and Star Center Tolerance gates are relaxed for large candidates (a proxy for large defocus). At large defocus a star becomes a hollow donut (the central-obstruction shadow): it has a big bounding box with a low pixel fill-ratio (which the strict Max Distortion would wrongly reject as too distorted) and a wobbly intensity-weighted center (which the strict centering test would wrongly reject as not centered). Small candidates (near focus) keep the strict thresholds, so junk is still rejected. Off by default; enable it if you collect autofocus frames far from focus and find defocused donut stars being dropped. The three Defocus-Aware tuning values below take effect only while this is enabled.
help.defocusDistortionSizeReference: Tuning knob for the Defocus-Aware Gates (only used while they are enabled). The candidate bounding-box size (in pixels, the larger of width/height) at or below which the strict gate thresholds still apply; larger candidates get the relaxed thresholds. Shared by both the distortion and centering relaxations. Lower it to relax smaller stars; raise it to keep more of the strict behavior. Default 30.
help.defocusDistortionMinFactor: Tuning knob for the Defocus-Aware Gates (only used while they are enabled). The floor multiplier applied to Max Distortion for very large (very defocused) candidates — the most permissive the distortion gate ever becomes. Must be greater than 0 and at most 1. Smaller values accept more heavily-distorted donuts. Default 0.25.
help.defocusCenteringToleranceFactor: Tuning knob for the Defocus-Aware Gates (only used while they are enabled). The maximum multiplier applied to Star Center Tolerance for very large (very defocused) candidates — the most permissive the centering gate ever becomes. Must be at least 1 (1 is a no-op; larger values relax centering further). Default 2.
help.defocusAwareStructure: When enabled, large/donut (heavily defocused) stars are kept during structure detection so they form candidates instead of being erased. The wavelet step that removes large-scale background structure (nebulae, gradients) can also erase a big out-of-focus donut entirely, so it never even becomes a candidate to evaluate. This option makes that removal coarser (by Structure Layer Boost extra layers) so large stars survive. Off by default (detection is unchanged); enable it together with a Structure Layer Boost above 0 if heavily-defocused stars are missing entirely (not just rejected). EARLY-stage setting.
help.structureLayerBoost: Only used while Defocus-Aware Structure is enabled. The number of extra wavelet layers added when removing large-scale structure, making the removal coarser so larger defocused donuts survive and form candidates. 0 means no change (identical to the feature being off). Raise it (1–6) if very out-of-focus stars never appear; raising it too far can let nebulosity/background structure leak in as false candidates. Default 0.
help.defocusAwareDonutDetection: MASTER toggle for defocus-aware donut detection (also on the optimizer wizard's start page). When ON, out-of-focus DONUT stars (heavily defocused stars that appear as hollow rings) are recovered: a morphological close reconnects fragmented rings and an annularity test lets a hollow ring pass the distortion gate like a filled disk (detection-only — it never changes HFR). It also unlocks the optimizer to tune ALL defocus-aware settings and to enable diffraction-spike / saturated-bloom suppression. Recommended for telescopes with a central obstruction (Newtonians/SCTs); leave OFF for refractors. Off by default; when OFF, detection is exactly as before.
help.donutMorphCloseSize: Only used while Defocus-Aware Donut Detection is on. Diameter (px) of the morphological-close kernel that reconnects fragmented donut-ring arcs into one candidate (the dominant cause of donuts being dropped as 'too small'). 1 means no close. Keep it smaller than the gap between a bright star's diffraction spikes so it doesn't bridge them. EARLY-stage setting. Default 5.
help.donutMinAnnularityHoleFraction: Only used while Defocus-Aware Donut Detection is on. Minimum size of a candidate's enclosed dark center (as a fraction of its bounding-box area) for it to count as a donut whose hole is filled for the distortion test — so a hollow ring is judged like a filled disk. This is detection-only and never changes the measured HFR/flux/center. Lower it to accept thinner rings; raise it to be stricter. Default 0.15.
help.donutMaxStreakEccentricity: Only used while Defocus-Aware Donut Detection is on. Rejects very LINEAR candidates (diffraction spikes from a bright star, or satellite/aircraft trails) when their elongation (eccentricity) meets or exceeds this value. 1.0 means OFF (a perfect line has eccentricity 1.0, so nothing is rejected); lower it toward 0.95 to enable. Round donuts measure well below this, so they are never affected. Default 1.0 (OFF — the optimizer enables it when you label false detections).
help.donutSaturationBloomRadius: Only used while Defocus-Aware Donut Detection is on. Rejects candidates whose center lies within this many pixels of a saturated star, removing the bloom/halo fragments around a bright saturated star while keeping the star itself. 0 means OFF. Default 0 (OFF — the optimizer enables it when you label the saturated star's artifacts as should-reject).
help.psfFitType: What type of PSF model to fit. Moffat 0.4 more closely resembles real stars and is the default used by PixInsight
help.psfResolution: The number of pixels of the width of a nominal square to sample star bounding boxes for the purposes of PSF model fitting. Higher resolution may be more accurate, but takes longer to calculate
help.psfParallelPartitionSize: Enables parallel processing of PSF modeling by partitioning the detected stars into batches of this size. Set to 0 to disable parallelism
help.psfFitThreshold: The minimum goodness of fit (R²) required for a PSF
help.usePSFAbsoluteDeviation: Enables an experimental PSF fitting approach that is more robust to noise and outlier pixels. This should more closely mimic PixInsight PSF fitting logic
help.hotpixelThreshold: A percentage representing the cutoff threshold for detecting a hotpixel. It's the percentage of full well difference between the 3x3 median blurred value and the pixel value
help.saturationThreshold: A percentage representing the cutoff threshold for detecting a saturated pixel. Star candidates containing saturated pixels are processed with those pixels masked during PSF fitting
help.excludeSaturatedStarsFromHFR: When enabled (default), partially-saturated stars (those whose peak reaches the Saturation Threshold) are left out of the per-frame HFR average — their flat, saturated cores bias HFR high and can pull the focus curve. The stars are still detected and counted; only the HFR average excludes them, and only while enough unsaturated stars remain. Disable to include every star's HFR as before.
help.contaminationSensitivity: How aggressively to flag stars whose background annulus is brighter on one side — a sign of a nearby star, hot column, or steep gradient. Value is the required asymmetry in multiples of the local background scatter (measured per star from the annulus itself); higher = fewer flags; 0 disables. Default 5.
help.rejectContaminatedStars: When enabled (default), stars flagged as contaminated are rejected outright so their one-sided contamination does not skew HFR and PSF statistics. When disabled, contaminated stars are kept and only flagged. A smooth one-sided background gradient (galaxy/nebula) is removed before the test, so only genuine localized contaminants trip it.
help.saveIntermediateImages: If enabled, every step of star detection emits a debugging file to the intermediate path
help.intermediateSavePath: When Save Intermediate Files is enabled, they are written to this path the next time star detection runs

tilter.sensorRotationDescription: Clockwise when facing the back of the camera
tilter.tilterScrewCountDescription: 3-screw plates use an equilateral layout, 4-screw plates one screw per sensor corner
tilter.fourScrewHint: Adjust opposing screws as a pair (loosen one, tighten the other) so the plate cannot bind
tilter.fourScrewApplyUnsupported: Applying to a device is only supported for 3-screw tilters
tilter.positiveTurnDirectionDescription: Which way a positive calculated value turns the screw on your adapter
tilter.startFromSeatedDescription: A fully seated screw can only be turned inward, so all values are shifted until one screw needs no turn and the others turn inward. This changes only backfocus, not tilt. Uncheck to show signed adjustments from the current position.

perihelion.title: Perihelion
perihelion.subtitle: Non-sidereal tracking for comets & asteroids — live orbital data, offline-durable.

about.heading: About Perihelion
about.description: Non-sidereal tracking for comets and asteroids -- sets a mount's custom RA/Dec rate live from current orbital elements, computed in-process with no external service.
about.dataSourcesDescription: Comet orbital elements come from the IAU Minor Planet Center, cached on-disk and synced on demand. Observed brightness cross-checks come from COBS (Comet OBServation database) where available. The orbital mechanics itself is built on CosineKitty.AstronomyEngine, the same engine (kept in version lockstep) OryxAstro's own website uses for its sky-events planner.
about.oryxAstroDescription: Perihelion is built by OryxAstro, whose website's own Deep Sky / Solar System Planner can send a tracking sequence for a comet or asteroid directly to PINS.
about.licenseText: GPL-3.0-or-later -- see the repository for the full text.

browse.step: Pick a comet or asteroid to track
browse.epochStaleTooltip: This object's orbital data may be less accurate than usual — tap for details.
browse.epochStaleLegendExplanation: This object's orbital elements are unusually far from their own reference epoch. Predicting a position this far from that anchor date relies on simple two-body physics that doesn't account for ongoing gravitational nudges from the planets, so the real position may drift from what's shown here.
browse.epochStaleLegendCaveat: This is a caution, not an error — the position shown is still the best available estimate. Syncing won't help if the underlying catalog entry itself hasn't been refit recently.
browse.observedTooltip: Real observer-reported brightness (COBS) vs. predicted Mag — green: brighter than predicted, amber/red: fainter.
browse.observedLegendBrighter: Green — brighter than predicted (a real outburst)
browse.selectedPrompt: Selected -- ready to check its position.

position.step: Review its position & compose the framing
position.pickFirst: Pick an object on the Browse tab first.
position.maxExposureExplanation: Comets move against the background stars. Tracking the mount on the comet's own rate -- whether via Quick Track or an Add to Sequence exposure loop -- means it's the stars that drift within each sub instead of the comet; once that drift passes about 1 pixel, stars start to elongate, which shows up as slightly egg-shaped stars and softer detail once you stack. This number is the exposure length at which that 1-pixel drift is reached, based on the comet's real angular rate and your camera's plate scale (pixel size and focal length).
position.maxExposureCaveat: It's a tracking limit only — it has no idea about sky background, light pollution, or your filter. Under a broadband (UV/IR-cut) filter at a brighter site, sky glow usually limits your real sub length well before this number does.
position.rateUnavailable: Set a camera pixel size and telescope focal length in this profile to see a max exposure.
position.observedBrightnessDescription: Real observer reports (COBS), average of the last {count} — vs. mag {predicted} predicted from orbital elements alone. Last reported {when}.
position.noLocation: No observer location set in this profile's Astrometry settings.
position.altitudeDescription: Uses {name}'s position right now for the whole night — real for a star, a slight approximation for a moving object, close enough for a transit curve.
position.pathDescription: Real path against the fixed stars — while tracking, {name} stays centered in-frame all night; this shows motion night to night, not movement within a single exposure. The two axes are stretched independently to fill this chart, so a small change in one can look bigger than it really is next to the other.

track.pickFirst: Pick an object on the Browse tab first.
track.liveStatusSubtitle: from the plugin itself, not just this page
track.guidingFailed: Tracking is running, but guiding could not be started: {error}
track.daytimeWarning: It's currently daytime at your site — there's nothing to see or guide on yet.
track.mountMismatchBody: Your mount is pointed about {deg}° away from {name}. What would you like to do?
track.guidingToggleDescription: Needed if you guide — otherwise it fights this drift.
track.autoReapplyToggleDescription: Quick Track only — recomputes and re-sends the rate on a timer, so a long unattended session stays accurate as the object's true rate drifts.
track.meridianFlipToggleDescription: Recommended on a GEM mount for anything running past the meridian.
track.autofocusToggleDescription: Refocuses on a timer during the imaging loop.
track.slewAndCenterDescriptionRest: points the mount at the target and plate-solves to confirm, using your existing framing rotation -- do this first if you haven't already found it another way (e.g. via Celestia Atlas).
track.eqmodToggleDescription: EQMOD reads RA rate as raw arcsec/sec instead of what NINA sends, making tracking ~15× too slow unless corrected. Only enable if your mount uses EQMOD.
track.eqmodDetectedHint: {name} looks like an EQMOD driver — you probably want this enabled.
track.reapplyIntervalDescription: How often Quick Track recomputes and resends the tracking rate. Default 900s (15 min) suits comets and asteroids; shorten it down to a 5-second floor for an object moving unusually fast.
track.addToSequenceDescriptionRest: appends a slew + track + imaging target to whatever sequence is already loaded in PINS's sequencer, for you to review and start -- your existing targets are untouched.
track.downloadSequenceDescriptionRest: saves an equivalent full sequence as a file instead of appending it to the loaded one -- for reviewing or importing later.
track.quickTrackDescriptionRest: sets the mount's rate directly right now — for manual or visual use, not a substitute for a real imaging sequence. Stops itself automatically if your mount reports it's reached the meridian flip limit, since Quick Track has no sequence trigger to flip it for you.
track.footer: Computed on-device from live orbital elements — comets and asteroids both sync periodically, then work offline.
track.guidingOnlyFallback: Mount can't take a custom rate -- tracking via guider shift only.
